```{python}
import polars as pl
import polars.selectors as cs
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, RandomForestRegressor, ExtraTreesRegressor
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, root_mean_squared_error, r2_score
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
```

```{python}
df = pl.read_csv("../dwellings_ml.csv")
df_neighborhoods = pl.read_csv("../dwellings_neighborhoods_ml.csv")
df_joined = df.join(
    df_neighborhoods,
    on="parcel",
    how="left"
)
```

```{python}
x = df_joined.select(cs.numeric().exclude(["yrbuilt", "before1980", "syear", "smonth"]))
y1 = df_joined.select("before1980")
y2 = df_joined.select("yrbuilt")

x_train1, x_test1, y_train1, y_test1 = train_test_split(
    x, y1, test_size=0.2, random_state=28
)
x_train2, x_test2, y_train2, y_test2 = train_test_split(
    x, y2, test_size=0.10, random_state=28
)
```

```{python}
rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=28)
rf_classifier.fit(x_train1, y_train1.to_numpy().ravel())
rfc_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test1)

print(metrics.classification_report(y_test1, rfc_pred))
```

```{python}
et_regressor = ExtraTreesRegressor(random_state=28)
et_regressor.fit(x_train2, y_train2.to_numpy().ravel())
etr_pred = et_regressor.predict(x_test2)

print("Extra Trees Regressor:")
print(f"MAE: {mean_absolute_error(y_test2, etr_pred)}")
print(f"RMSE: {root_mean_squared_error(y_test2, etr_pred)}")
print(f"R^2: {r2_score(y_test2, etr_pred)}")
etr_abs_errors = abs(etr_pred - y_test2.to_numpy().ravel())
print(f"More than 5 years off: {(etr_abs_errors > 5).mean():.1%}")
print(f"More than 10 years off: {(etr_abs_errors > 10).mean():.1%}")
```

Report: 
On average the Mean average error of the model is 6.16 years with the Root mean squared error being 13 years off pointing to a model that makes some really large mistakes but gets most guesses close to the actual year they were built. The R Squared error is 0.87 meaning the model explains 87% of the outcome variation with only 13% unexplained, so I would say it's an okay model for estimating home age. It has problems and to get the RMSE down I need more dwellings or features that are better tells of home age such as if it has a brick exterior or not. ## Controlled comparison

The control set contains 20% of the unique parcels. All records for those parcels
are held out of training. The parcel split is saved so rerunning this comparison
uses the same properties. Every model is evaluated on the same original dwelling
rows, joined to one neighborhood record per parcel. Training is compared with
and without the extra copies created by the original neighborhood join.

These control scores are for comparing experiments. After choosing a model,
final performance should be checked on another independent set of properties.

```{python}
import json
from pathlib import Path
from sklearn.base import clone

control_dwellings = pl.read_csv("../dwellings_ml.csv")
control_neighborhoods = pl.read_csv("../dwellings_neighborhoods_ml.csv")
unique_neighborhoods = control_neighborhoods.unique(subset=["parcel"])

# Reuse this saved split for every model and both training joins.
split_path = Path("unit4_stretch_control_split.json")
all_parcels = sorted(control_dwellings["parcel"].unique().to_list())

if split_path.exists():
    parcel_split = json.loads(split_path.read_text())
else:
    training_parcels, control_parcels = train_test_split(
        all_parcels, test_size=0.2, random_state=28
    )
    parcel_split = {
        "training_parcels": sorted(training_parcels),
        "control_parcels": sorted(control_parcels)
    }
    split_path.write_text(json.dumps(parcel_split, indent=2) + "\n")

training_parcels = parcel_split["training_parcels"]
control_parcels = parcel_split["control_parcels"]
assert not set(training_parcels) & set(control_parcels)
assert set(training_parcels) | set(control_parcels) == set(all_parcels)

training_source = control_dwellings.filter(pl.col("parcel").is_in(training_parcels))
control_source = control_dwellings.filter(pl.col("parcel").is_in(control_parcels))

# Multiple original records for a parcel stay together in the same set.
control_set = control_source.join(
    unique_neighborhoods, on="parcel", how="left", validate="m:1"
)
training_original_join = training_source.join(
    control_neighborhoods, on="parcel", how="left"
)
training_corrected_join = training_source.join(
    unique_neighborhoods, on="parcel", how="left", validate="m:1"
)
assert control_set.height == control_source.height
assert training_corrected_join.height == training_source.height

control_features = control_set.select(
    cs.numeric().exclude(["yrbuilt", "before1980", "syear", "smonth"])
).columns
x_control = control_set.select(control_features)
y_control = control_set["yrbuilt"].to_numpy()

print(f"Training parcels: {len(training_parcels):,}")
print(f"Control parcels: {len(control_parcels):,}")
print(f"Control dwelling rows: {control_set.height:,}")
print(f"Original-join training rows: {training_original_join.height:,}")
print(f"Corrected-join training rows: {training_corrected_join.height:,}")
```

```{python}
# Include a random forest baseline and the two Extra Trees configurations above.
# Each configuration is kept identical between the two training joins.
control_models = {
    "Random forest baseline": RandomForestRegressor(random_state=28),
    "Extra Trees baseline": clone(et_regressor),
    "Extra Trees alternative": clone(et_regressor2)
}
control_results = []

for join_name, training_data in [
    ("Original join", training_original_join),
    ("Corrected join", training_corrected_join)
]:
    x_training = training_data.select(control_features)
    y_training = training_data["yrbuilt"].to_numpy()

    for model_name, model_template in control_models.items():
        control_model = clone(model_template).set_params(n_jobs=-1)
        control_model.fit(x_training, y_training)
        control_predictions = control_model.predict(x_control)
        control_errors = abs(control_predictions - y_control)

        control_results.append({
            "training_join": join_name,
            "model": model_name,
            "MAE": mean_absolute_error(y_control, control_predictions),
            "RMSE": root_mean_squared_error(y_control, control_predictions),
            "R_squared": r2_score(y_control, control_predictions),
            "percent_over_5": 100 * (control_errors > 5).mean(),
            "percent_over_10": 100 * (control_errors > 10).mean()
        })

control_comparison = pl.DataFrame(control_results)
with pl.Config(tbl_cols=-1, fmt_str_lengths=100, float_precision=3):
    display(control_comparison.sort(["model", "training_join"]))
```

## Tuned regression model

The tuning script compared 20 model and feature configurations, including
random forests, Extra Trees, gradient boosting, both training joins, and derived
features. Tree ensembles were also compared using their mean, median, and a
prediction based on the densest interval of tree estimates. The strongest
candidates were checked on three parcel-separated validation splits.

Selection prioritized the percentage more than ten years off, followed by the
percentage more than five years off and MAE. A lower error count can come with
larger remaining mistakes, so RMSE is reported too. The saved control parcels
were excluded from this tuning sweep; they have been evaluated earlier in the
project, so they are not a wholly untouched external test.

The ensemble experiments use 150 trees. The comparison includes alternatives
selected for lowest validation MAE and fewest five-year misses, as well as the
primary ten-year target. The interval-based rules are experimental ways to
combine predictions; they do not guarantee an individual home's error bound.

Run `../../.venv/bin/python tune_regression.py` from this directory to repeat the
search. This section only fits the saved winner, rather than repeating the search.

```{python}
from tune_regression import (
    load_data,
    training_rows,
    features as tuning_features,
    make_model,
    predict_selected,
    metrics as regression_scores
)

selected_settings = json.loads(Path("unit4_stretch_best_model.json").read_text())
tuned_data, tuned_neighborhoods = load_data()
tuned_split = json.loads(Path("unit4_stretch_control_split.json").read_text())
tuned_spec = selected_settings["spec"]
# Use "median" for the lowest-MAE option, or "window5" for the five-year target.
tuned_aggregation = selected_settings["aggregation"]

tuned_training = training_rows(
    tuned_data,
    tuned_neighborhoods,
    tuned_split["training_parcels"],
    tuned_spec["training"]
)
tuned_control = tuned_data.filter(
    pl.col("parcel").is_in(tuned_split["control_parcels"])
)
assert not set(tuned_training["parcel"]) & set(tuned_control["parcel"])

tuned_regressor = make_model(tuned_spec)
tuned_regressor.fit(
    tuning_features(tuned_training, tuned_spec["features"]),
    tuned_training["yrbuilt"].to_numpy()
)
tuned_predictions = predict_selected(
    tuned_regressor,
    tuning_features(tuned_control, tuned_spec["features"]),
    tuned_aggregation
)
tuned_scores = regression_scores(tuned_control["yrbuilt"].to_numpy(), tuned_predictions)

print(f"Selected model: {tuned_spec['name']}")
print(tuned_regressor)
print(f"Combining tree predictions: {tuned_aggregation}")
print(f"MAE: {tuned_scores['MAE']:.3f}")
print(f"RMSE: {tuned_scores['RMSE']:.3f}")
print(f"R^2: {tuned_scores['R_squared']:.3f}")
print(f"More than 5 years off: {tuned_scores['percent_over_5']:.1f}%")
print(f"More than 10 years off: {tuned_scores['percent_over_10']:.1f}%")

# Every row in this comparison uses the identical held-out dwelling records.
tuning_report = json.loads(Path("unit4_stretch_tuning_control.json").read_text())
with pl.Config(tbl_cols=-1, fmt_str_lengths=100, float_precision=3):
    display(pl.DataFrame(tuning_report["results"]))
```
